'''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''' (月夜見宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=shrine}} located in Miyago, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm">辰巳出版（2013）：16ページ</ref>. It is a [[:en:Betsugū|Betsugū]] of [[Ise Grand Shrine|Ise Jingu]] {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine)<ref name="tm" /><ref name="ik">伊勢文化舎 編（2008）：39ページ</ref><ref name="mr">みらい出版（2013）：64ページ</ref><ref name="gk">学研パブリッシング（2013）：69ページ</ref><ref name="rg">JTBパブリッシング（2011）：42ページ</ref><ref name="rb">出版事業本部 国内情報部 第三編集部 編（2014）：34ページ</ref><ref name="as">三橋（2013）：124ページ</ref>。 It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

== Overview ==
[[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Aerial view of Tsukiyomi-no-Miya]]

Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is an auxiliary shrine (betsugu) of the Outer Shrine (Geku), located about 300 meters north of Geku and approximately 500 meters west of {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station}}. It enshrines two deities within the same shrine building: {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ja|月夜見尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ツクヨミ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q595520}} (Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) and his fierce spirit, '''Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto-no-Aramitama''' (荒御魂 of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto) <ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/>.

Unlike the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Naikū)|ja|月讀宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}} auxiliary shrine of the Inner Shrine (Naiku), where Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto and his Aramitama are enshrined separately, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya uniquely houses both deities within a single structure <ref name="rb"/>. The only other auxiliary shrines that enshrine two deities in one building are {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|ja|風宮}} (Kaze-no-Miya) of the Outer Shrine and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|ja|風日祈宮|lt=Kazahi-no-Miya}} of the Inner Shrine, both enshrining Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto (級長津彦命) and Shinatsuhime-no-Mikoto (級長戸辺命).

Tsukiyomi-no-Miya is the only auxiliary shrine of the Outer Shrine located outside the main precincts <ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/><ref name="as"/>. Despite being in the urban area of Ise City, its grounds maintain a serene atmosphere <ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/>. The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River (Mie Prefecture)}} <ref name="ik"/><ref name="gk"/>.

The {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|ja|三重県道37号鳥羽松阪線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 37|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357923}} runs along the northern side of the moat and serves as the route for the '''Hatsuhobiki''' (初穂曳), a festival procession held every October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}. During this event, decorated carts carry the first harvested rice offerings to the Outer Shrine.

Adjacent to the right rear of the shrine building is the auxiliary shrine of {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社}} <ref name="ik"/>. To the left rear stands an {{ill|Inari Ōkami|ja|稲荷|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 稲荷神|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q719665}} <ref name="tm"/>, and to the right is a large sacred camphor tree (大楠), where many people offer prayers <ref name="rg"/>. Like other auxiliary shrines outside the main precincts, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya has a '''Shukueiya''' (宿衛屋), a guardhouse where Shinto priests are present during visiting hours to distribute amulets, offer kagura performances, and manage food offerings (御饌).

== Festivals ==
The shrine follows a festival schedule similar to that of {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮}}, with offerings from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ar|البيت الإمبراطوري في اليابان|as|জাপানৰ ৰাজপৰিয়াল|ast|Familia imperial xaponesa|az|Yaponiya imperator evi|be|Імператарскі дом Японіі|ca|Família Imperial del Japó|ckb|خێزانی شاھانەی ژاپۆن|cs|Japonská císařská dynastie|de|Japanisches Kaiserhaus|el|Αυτοκρατορικός Οίκος της Ιαπωνίας|eo|Japana reĝa familio|es|Familia imperial japonesa|fa|دودمان یاماتو|fr|Maison impériale du Japon|he|בית הקיסרות של יפן|hr|Japanska carska obitelj|hu|Japán császári ház|id|Wangsa Kekaisaran Jepang|it|Famiglia imperiale del Giappone|ja|皇室|ko|일본 황실|la|Domus imperatoriae Iaponiae|ms|Kerabat diraja Jepun|no|Japans keiserhus|pt|Casa Imperial do Japão|ro|Familia imperială a Japoniei|ru|Японский императорский дом|sh|Carska kuća Japana|simple|Imperial House of Japan|sq|Shtëpia Perandorake e Japonisë|th|ราชวงศ์ญี่ปุ่น|tr|Yamato Hanedanı|uk|Імператорський дім Японії|ur|جاپان کا شاہی خاندان|vi|Hoàng thất Nhật Bản|zh|日本皇室|zh_classical|日本皇室|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún hông-sek|zh_yue|日本皇室|qid=Q909452|lt=Imperial House of Japan}} during prayers for the harvest (*{{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}*), seasonal festivals (*{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}}*), and major thanksgiving ceremonies (*{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}* and *{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}*).

* '''January'''
**{{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}* (New Year's Festival) – {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1}}  
*** A festival celebrating the new year and praying for the eternal prosperity of the imperial lineage.
**{{ill|Genshi-sai|ja|元始祭}}* (Imperial Foundation Festival) – {{ill|January 3|en|January 3|qid=Q2156|lt=January 3}}  
*** A festival celebrating the origins of the imperial rule.

* '''February'''
**{{ill|Kenkoku Kinen-sai|ja|建国記念祭}}* (National Foundation Festival) – {{ill|February 11|en|February 11|qid=Q2335|lt=February 11}}  
*** Celebrating the founding of Japan by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}}.
**{{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinensai}}* (Prayer Festival) – {{ill|February 18|en|February 18|qid=Q2343|lt=February 18}}  
*** A ceremony held early in the year to pray for abundant grain harvests and national peace.
**{{ill|The Emperor's Birthday|ja|天長祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenchō-sai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 天皇誕生日|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q72318}}* (Emperor’s Birthday Festival) – {{ill|February 23|en|February 23|qid=Q2352|lt=February 23}}  
*** A festival honoring the birthday of {{ill|Naruhito|ja|徳仁天皇|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Naruhito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 徳仁|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q217096}}.

* '''May'''
**{{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|May 14|en|May 14|qid=Q2561|lt=May 14}}  
*** Offerings are made at the Outer Shrine, Inner Shrine, and affiliated shrines to pray for protection from storms and a bountiful harvest.

* '''June'''
**{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|June 18|en|June 18|qid=Q2670|lt=June 18}}–{{ill|June 19|en|June 19|qid=Q2669|lt=June 19}}  
*** A biannual festival held in June and December to pray for the well-being of the nation and the emperor. Together with *{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}*, these are called the *Three Great Festivals* (三節祭 or 三時祭).

* '''August'''
**{{ill|Kazahi-no-Misai|ja|風日祈祭|2=ja|3=風日祈祭|qid=Q135524493|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazahinomi-sai|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135524493}}* (Wind and Sun Festival) – {{ill|August 4|en|August 4|qid=Q2784|lt=August 4}}  
*** A repetition of the May festival to pray for good weather and agricultural prosperity.

* '''October'''
**{{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}* (First Fruits Festival) – {{ill|October 18|en|October 18|qid=Q2964|lt=October 18}}–{{ill|October 19|en|October 19|qid=Q2961|lt=October 19}}  
*** A festival where priests present freshly harvested grains as offerings to the gods.

* '''November'''
**{{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|en|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niinamesai}}* (New Harvest Festival) – {{ill|November 24|en|November 24|qid=Q3022|lt=November 24}}  
*** A festival in which the emperor offers the season’s first grains to the gods and partakes in them as an act of gratitude.

* '''December'''
**{{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}}* (Monthly Festival) – {{ill|December 18|en|December 18|qid=Q2438|lt=December 18}}–{{ill|December 19|en|December 19|qid=Q2451|lt=December 19}}

* {{ill|March 1|en|March 1|qid=Q2393|lt=March 1}} - {{ill|Ōmike|ja|大御饌}}（おおみけ）・{{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}}

Above, the {{ill|Ritchūsai|ja|立柱祭}}, {{ill|raising ceremony|ja|上棟祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōtōsai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上棟式|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q106351734}}, {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|杵築祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotsukisai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}}, {{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|ja|後鎮祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gochinsai|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神宮式年遷宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3959472}}, {{ill|Sengyo|ja|遷御}}, and {{ill|Hōhei|ja|奉幣}} were scheduled according to the divine decision (*{{ill|Gojijō|ja|御治定}}*) of the reigning emperor<ref name="sg"/>。 

Additionally, on {{ill|February 22|en|February 22|qid=Q2351|lt=February 22}}, the *{{ill|Oshiraishimochi|ja|お白石持|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshiraishi-mochi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q17225061}}* ceremony took place, during which approximately 1,000 participants from the {{ill|Miyago Hōkendan|ja|宮後奉献団}} carried sacred stones (*{{ill|Oshiraishi|ja|御白石}}*) in a cart from the {{ill|Urakuchi Intersection|ja|浦口交差点}} to {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Geku)|ja|月夜見宮|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Miya}}, covering a distance of 1.2 km<ref name="cn1502">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=次代につなぐ「エンヤ」 伊勢・月夜見宮でお白石持行事|author=中平雄大|publisher=[[中日新聞]]|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}</ref>。 This marked the Completion tier 5]]  
A '''narrow, 4-meter-wide straight path''' connects the '''North Gate (北御門, Kita-mikado) of the Outer Shrine''' to '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya'''. This road is known as '''"Kamiji Street" (神路通り, Kamiji-dōri), meaning "Path of the Gods,"''' as it is '''believed to be the route taken by deities.'''  

See {{ill|Kamiji Street|ja|神路通り|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamiji Street|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q30114580}} for details.

== Worshipers' Association (信者団体) ==
In '''1960 (Shōwa 35)''', a group of '''Ise City residents''' founded the '''Tsukiyomi-{{ill|Kō (lecture)|en|Kō (lecture)|qid=Q11632184|lt=kō}} (月夜見講)''', which was later renamed the '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Hōsankai (月夜見宮奉賛会, Tsukiyomi-no-Miya Worshipers' Association).'''  
- This organization '''holds annual thanksgiving festivals''' on '''April 19 and September 19''', among other activities.

== Access (交通) ==
* '''Train:'''
** '''10-minute walk''' from '''{{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise City Station}}''' (served by '''JR {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangu Line}}''' & '''Kintetsu {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line}}''').  
** '''5-minute walk''' from the '''North Gate of the Outer Shrine''' via '''Kamiji Street'''.  

* '''Bus:'''
** '''3-minute walk''' from '''Shindō Bus Stop''' ('''{{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} Bus''').  
** '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae Bus Stop''' (served by the '''{{ill|Q11379021|ja|伊勢市コミュニティバス|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise City Community Bus|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379021}}''').  
** Note: From '''July 20, 2013''', the '''Sangu Bus''' operated by Mie Kotsu stopped at '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya-mae''', but this service was '''discontinued on March 31, 2015'''.  

* '''Car:'''
** '''Approx. 3 km''' from '''{{ill|Ise interchange|ja|伊勢インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Interchange|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884857}} (Ise Expressway).'''  
** '''Parking:''' There are '''only 2-4 parking spaces in front of the torii gate''', but '''metered parking''' is available on the south side of the street.

== Shrine Grounds (境内) ==
* '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (月夜見宮)''' - A '''Betsugū''' (auxiliary shrine) of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}} (Outer Shrine of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}). The shrine’s '''architecture follows Shinmei-zukuri''' and features '''chigi (forked finials) cut horizontally''' and '''five katsuogi (short decorative logs)''', '''a thatched roof''', and '''a south-facing orientation'''.  
** '''Shikinen Sengu (式年遷宮)''': The shrine is '''reconstructed every 20 years''' according to the ancient practice of '''Shikinen Sengu'''. The '''former shrine grounds''' (古殿地, kodenchi) are located directly to the east and west of the current shrine.  
** '''Traditional Legend''': It is said that in the past, when the people of '''Miyago Town''' were carrying '''sacred timber (役木, yakugi)''' for shrine reconstruction, they '''passed through Yokaichiba Town'''. At that moment, '''a fire broke out in Miyago Town''', and the timber carriers '''rushed back to extinguish it'''. As a result, the people of Yokaichiba took over the role of '''carrying the sacred timber'''. Since then, in the '''Okihikizome-shiki (御木曳初式, First Timber-Carrying Ceremony)''', '''the people of Yokaichiba''' have traditionally taken on the '''honor of bringing the sacred timber to Tsukiyomi-no-Miya'''.  

* '''{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|ja|高河原神社}}''' - Dedicated to '''Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto no Mitama (月夜見尊御魂, Spirit of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto)'''. Though located within '''Tsukiyomi-no-Miya''', it is actually '''a Sessha (摂社, auxiliary shrine) of Toyōke Daijingū (Outer Shrine).'''  

* '''{{ill|Inari shrine|fa|معبد ایناری|fr|Sanctuaire Inari|ja|稲荷神社|ko|이나리 신사|simple|Inari shrine|uk|Святилище Інарі|qid=Q514480}}''' – A shrine dedicated to '''Inari''', the deity of '''prosperity and agriculture'''.  

* '''Shukueya (宿衛屋)''' – A '''guardhouse''' for shrine officials.

**Tsukiyomi-no-miya** (つきよみのみや) is a Shinto shrine in Miyago, {{ill|Ise, Mie|ar|إيسه|azb|ایسه، میه|bcl|Ise, Mie|be|Ісэ (горад)|ca|Ise (ciutat japonesa)|ce|Исе (гӀала)|ckb|ئیسێ|cs|Ise (Mie)|de|Ise (Mie)|eo|Ise (urbo)|es|Ise (Mie)|et|Ise (Jaapan)|eu|Ise (Mie)|fa|ایسه، میه|fi|Ise (kaupunki)|fr|Ise (Mie)|gl|Ise|hr|Ise|hy|Իսե (քաղաք)|id|Ise, Mie|it|Ise (Giappone)|ja|伊勢市|ka|ისე|ko|이세시|lt|Isė (Japonija)|mg|Ise|mzn|ایسه، میه|nl|Ise (Mie)|no|Ise (Mie)|pl|Ise (Japonia)|pt|Ise (Japão)|ro|Ise, Japonia|ru|Исе (город)|sh|Ise|simple|Ise, Mie|sr|Исе|sv|Ise, Japan|szl|Ise (Japůńijo)|tg|Исе|tl|Ise, Mie|tr|Ise (şehir)|tt|Исе (шәһәр)|uk|Ісе (Міє)|ur|ایسے، میہ|uz|Ise (Mie)|vi|Ise, Mie|war|Ise, Mie|zh|伊勢市|zh_classical|伊勢市|zh_min_nan|Ise-chhī|zh_yue|伊勢|qid=Q328067}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}.<ref name="tm"/> It is a betsugu (auxiliary shrine) of the Outer Shrine (Gekū), {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮|tok|tomo sewi suli Keku|zh|豐受大神宮|qid=Q11633343}}, of the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}} complex.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 16</ref><ref name="ik">Ise Bunkasha, ed. (2008): p. 39</ref><ref name="mr">Mirai Publishing (2013): p. 64</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 69</ref><ref name="rg">JTB Publishing (2011): p. 42</ref><ref name="rb">Publishing Business Headquarters, Domestic Information Dept., Third Editorial Dept., ed. (2014): p. 34</ref><ref name="as">Mitsuhashi (2013): p. 124</ref> It is also a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=**Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto**}} (つきよみのみこと)<ref name="tm" /><ref name="ik" /><ref name="mr" /><ref name="gk" /><ref name="rg" /><ref name="rb" /><ref name="as" />

**{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aramitama of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto}}** (つきよみのみことのあらみたま)<ref name="tm" /><ref name="ik" /><ref name="mr" /><ref name="gk" /><ref name="rg" /><ref name="rb" /><ref name="as" />

:Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto is the same deity as Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, who is enshrined at Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月讀宮), a betsugu of the Inner Shrine (Naikū).<ref name="mr" /><ref name="gk" /><ref name="rb" /><ref name="as" /> He is also said to be the younger brother of {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602}}.<ref name="tm" /><ref name="gk" /><ref name="as" /> Because people historically planned farm work using a lunar calendar ({{ill|Lunar calendar|Q185688|qid=Q185688}}) based on the waxing and waning of the moon, he has been regarded as a deity connected with agriculture.<ref name="mr" /><ref name="rg" /> He is also considered a river deity of Takagawara<ref name="ik" /> and a deity connected with women as well.<ref name="mr" /><ref name="rg" /> In *Shinmei Hisho*, the sacred object ({{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}) is described as a {{ill|Mirror|Q35197|qid=Q35197}}.<ref name="as" />

=== Overview ===
[[File:Tsukiyomi-nomiya(Geku)_00.JPG|thumb|300px|right|Tsukiyomi-no-miya seen from above]]
Tsukiyomi-no-miya is a betsugu of the Outer Shrine located about 300 m north of the Gekū and about 500 m west of {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748}}. Two deities—{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto}} and his aramitama (rough/active spirit), **Aramitama of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto**—are enshrined together in the same shrine building.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/> At Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月讀宮), a betsugu of the Inner Shrine, Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto and his aramitama are enshrined in separate buildings, but at Tsukiyomi-no-miya (月夜見宮) they are enshrined together, which is a distinguishing feature.<ref name="rb"/> Other betsugu that enshrine two deities in a single building include {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|Q11665463|qid=Q11665463}} (an Outer Shrine betsugu) and {{ill|Kazahinomi-no-Miya|Q11665488|qid=Q11665488}} (an Inner Shrine betsugu), both of which enshrine Shinatsuhiko-no-Mikoto and Shinatobe-no-Mikoto.

Among the Outer Shrine’s betsugu, this is the only shrine located outside the main sacred precinct (miyagi).<ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/><ref name="as"/> Although it stands in the urban area of Ise, the grounds retain a quiet atmosphere.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg"/> The moat surrounding three sides of the precinct is thought to be a remnant of a tributary of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|Q6884164|qid=Q6884164}}.<ref name="ik"/><ref name="gk"/> {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 37|Q11357923|qid=Q11357923}}, which runs along the north side of the moat, becomes the venue for **{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hatsuhiki}}** (the “Oise Grand Festival”) held each October in conjunction with the {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045}}, and the ceremonial carts carrying first fruits into the Outer Shrine pass through.

The Outer Shrine’s sessha (subsidiary shrine), **{{ill|Takagawara Shrine|Q17225931|qid=Q17225931}}**, is located behind the right side of the main shrine building.<ref name="ik"/> Behind the left side, an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari}} is enshrined.<ref name="tm"/> To the right stands a large camphor tree, where some visitors offer prayers.<ref name="rg"/> As with other outlying betsugu, there is a **shukueiya** (a station where shrine staff stay during visiting hours), which distributes amulets and talismans and arranges kagura performances and offerings.

=== History ===
Its origins are not certain, but it is said that in ancient times it was called **Takagawara** and was a shrine that enshrined an agricultural deity. In the *Engishiki* compiled in 927 (the 5th year of Engi) during the reign of the 60th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}, it was ranked first among the Outer Shrine’s sessha. In the *Toyuke-no-miya Gishikichō* it is recorded as “Tsukuyomi Shrine,” in the *Engishiki Jinmyōchō* as “Tsukiyomi Shrine,” and in the *Ise Daijingū Shiki* as “Tsukiyomi Sha.”<ref name="as"/> In 1210 (the 4th year of Jōgen), it was elevated to the status of a betsugu.<ref name="gk"/><ref name="as2">Mitsuhashi (2013): p. 125</ref>

In the Meiji period, the Outer Shrine betsugu “tsukiyomi-no-miya” came to be written as **月夜見宮**, while the Inner Shrine betsugu “tsukiyomi-no-miya” came to be written as **月讀宮**.<ref name="tm"/> During the {{ill|Ise Riot|Q11379085|qid=Q11379085}} of 1876 (Meiji 9), nearby towns burned, and because of concern that the fire might spread to Tsukiyomi-no-miya, the sacred object ({{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}) was temporarily moved to {{ill|Kaze-no-Miya|Q11665463|qid=Q11665463}}.<ref>Kaneko (1983): p. 214</ref> During the {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}}, the {{ill|Ujiyamada Air Raid|Q18990749|qid=Q18990749}} occurred on July 29, 1945 (Shōwa 20). Although all surrounding houses burned down, due to desperate firefighting by the {{ill|Military|Q8473|qid=Q8473}} and the fact that an incendiary bomb lodged in the thatched roof failed to explode, only the shrine buildings of Tsukiyomi-no-miya remained standing amid the ruins.<ref>Yano (2006): pp. 184–185</ref> However, a contracted shukueiin (guard attendant) was killed in the air raid, and the miyatsukasa (shrine official) suffered severe burns.<ref>Yano (2006): p. 185</ref>

=== Festivals ===
Rites comparable to those of the Inner Shrine are performed, and for the Kinensai, Tsukinamisai, Kannamesai, and Niinamesai, offerings ({{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}}) are presented from the {{ill|Imperial House of Japan|ar|البيت الإمبراطوري في اليابان|as|জাপানৰ ৰাজপৰিয়াল|ast|Familia imperial xaponesa|az|Yaponiya imperator evi|be|Імператарскі дом Японіі|ca|Família Imperial del Japó|ckb|خێزانی شاھانەی ژاپۆن|cs|Japonská císařská dynastie|de|Japanisches Kaiserhaus|el|Αυτοκρατορικός Οίκος της Ιαπωνίας|eo|Japana reĝa familio|es|Familia imperial japonesa|fa|دودمان یاماتو|fr|Maison impériale du Japon|he|בית הקיסרות של יפן|hr|Japanska carska obitelj|hu|Japán császári ház|id|Wangsa Kekaisaran Jepang|it|Famiglia imperiale del Giappone|ja|皇室|ko|일본 황실|la|Domus imperatoriae Iaponiae|ms|Kerabat diraja Jepun|no|Japans keiserhus|pt|Casa Imperial do Japão|ro|Familia imperială a Japoniei|ru|Японский императорский дом|sh|Carska kuća Japana|simple|Imperial House of Japan|sq|Shtëpia Perandorake e Japonisë|th|ราชวงศ์ญี่ปุ่น|tr|Yamato Hanedanı|uk|Імператорський дім Японії|ur|جاپان کا شاہی خاندان|vi|Hoàng thất Nhật Bản|zh|日本皇室|zh_classical|日本皇室|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún hông-sek|zh_yue|日本皇室|qid=Q909452}}.
* January
** Saitansai (New Year’s Day Festival) (January 1) A festival celebrating the New Year and praying for the eternal continuity of the imperial line.
** Genshisai (January 3) A festival celebrating the origin of the imperial succession at the start of the year.
* February
** Kenkoku Kinen-sai (National Foundation Festival) (February 11) A festival celebrating the founding of the nation by {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}.
** Kinensai (February 18) A festival held at the beginning of the year praying for abundant harvests and national peace.
** Tenchōsai (February 23) A festival celebrating the birthday of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Emperor Naruhito}}.
* May
** Kazahinomisai (May 14) A rite in which offerings are presented not only at the Outer and Inner Shrines but also at betsugu, massha, and sessha, praying that there will be no damage from wind and rain and that the five grains will be abundant.
* June
** Tsukinamisai (June 18–19) A festival held in June and December on the 11th, praying for national peace and the emperor’s well-being; at the Shrine it is also called one of the “Three Seasonal Festivals” together with the Kannamesai.
* August
** Kazahinomisai (August 4) Same as above.
* October
** {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|id|Festival Kannamesai|ja|神嘗祭|ko|신상제 (10월)|qid=Q11255045}} (October 18–19) A festival in which priests offer newly harvested grain as sacred food ({{ill|Shinsen|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=Ōmike}}).
* November
** {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}} (November 24) A festival in which the emperor offers newly harvested grain to the gods, partakes of it himself, and gives thanks for the harvest.
* December
** Tsukinamisai (December 18–19)

=== Shikinen sengū ===
[[File:Sengu of Tsukiyomi no Miya, August 2014.jpg|thumb|Tsukiyomi-no-miya before the Ritchūsai (photo taken August 11, 2014)<br/>Left: the then-current shrine building; right: the shrine building under construction]]
The ceremonies and schedule for the 62nd shikinen sengū of Tsukiyomi-no-miya are as follows:<ref name="ik1503">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|title=Another “moon deity” of Ise Grand Shrine’s Outer Shrine betsugu also moves—only Kaze-no-miya remains|publisher=Ise-Shima Keizai Shimbun|date=2015-03-03|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307142246/http://iseshima.keizai.biz/headline/2259/|archivedate=2015-03-07}}</ref><ref name="sg">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|title=Relocations of 12 betsugu including Tsukiyomi-no-miya - Ise Grand Shrine|publisher=Jingu Administration Office|accessdate=2015-03-07|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210061619/http://www.isejingu.or.jp/sikinen_2.html|archivedate=2015-02-10}}</ref>

**2014**
* August 20 – Ritchūsai (Pillar-Raising Festival) / Jōtōsai (Ridgepole-Raising Festival)
* October 5 – Nokitsukesai (Eaves-Attaching Festival)
* November 5 – Irakasai (Roofing Festival)
**2015**
* February 26 – Mitosai / Mifunashiro Hōnōshiki / Araikiyome
* February 27 – Kotsukisai / Gochinsai / Kawara Ōharae
* February 28 – Okazari / Sengyo (Transfer of the deity)
* March 1 – Ōmike / Hōhei

Among these, the Ritchūsai, Jōtōsai, Kotsukisai, Gochinsai, Sengyo, and Hōhei are conducted according to dates determined by imperial decision.<ref name="sg"/> In addition, on February 22, 2015, the **Oshiraishi-mochi** event was held, in which about 1,000 people of the Miyago offering group pulled ceremonial carts loaded with sacred white stones for 1.2 km from the Uraguchi intersection to Tsukiyomi-no-miya.<ref name="cn1502">{{Cite web|ja|url=http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|title=“Enya” linking to the next generation: Oshiraishi-mochi event at Tsukiyomi-no-miya in Ise|author=Yudai Nakahira|publisher=Chunichi Shimbun|date=2015-02-23|accessdate=2015-03-08|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150307161058/http://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/mie/20150223/CK2015022302000028.html|archivedate=2015-03-07}}</ref> With this, all oshiraishi-mochi events for the betsugu were completed.<ref name="cn1502"/>

=== Precincts ===
* Tsukiyomi-no-miya — A betsugu of the Outer Shrine (Gekū) of the Ise Grand Shrine complex. In keeping with the Outer Shrine, the thatched **shinmei-zukuri** building faces south and has outward-cut chigi and five (an odd number) katsuogi. The old site for relocation (kodenchi) lies adjacent to it east–west. As with the Outer Shrine, a relocation ({{ill|Jingū Shikinen Sengū|Q3959472|qid=Q3959472}}) is performed once every 20 years. There is a tradition that when people of Miyago pulled the “yakukan” (construction timber) and reached Yōkaichiba-chō, a fire broke out in Miyago, and the pullers returned to fight it; the people of Yōkaichiba-chō took over pulling the timber, and ever since, at the **{{ill|Okihiki|Q11489125|qid=Q11489125}}** the people of Yōkaichiba-chō have pulled and offered the timber to Tsukiyomi-no-miya.
* {{ill|Takagawara Shrine|Q17225931|qid=Q17225931}} — Enshrined deity: the mitama (spirit) of Tsukiyomi-no-Mikoto. Located within the precincts of Tsukiyomi-no-miya, but it is a sessha of Toyouke Daijingu (the Outer Shrine) of Ise Grand Shrine.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Inari Shrine}}
* Shukueiya

=== Kamiji Street ===
[[File:Kamiji Street from Tsukiyomi no Miya.jpg|thumb|Kamiji Street]]
The straight road about 4 m wide running from the Outer Shrine’s Kita-mikado (North Gate) to Tsukiyomi-no-miya is regarded as “the road the gods pass,” and is called **Kamiji Street** (神路通り). See the article {{ill|Kamiji Street|Q30114580|qid=Q30114580}}.

=== Devotee organization ===
In 1960 (Shōwa 35), a Tsukiyomi confraternity (Tsukiyomi-kō) was formed mainly by worshippers living in Ise, later renamed the Tsukiyomi-no-miya Hōsankai. The Hōsankai carries out activities such as holding a festival of gratitude for divine blessings on April 19 and September 19 each year.

=== Access ===
* About a 10-minute walk from {{ill|Iseshi Station|eo|Stacio Iseshi|fr|Gare d'Iseshi|id|Stasiun Iseshi|ja|伊勢市駅|jv|Setatsiyun Iseshi|ko|이세시역|my|အိဆဲရှိဘူတာ|ur|ایسیشی اسٹیشن|zh|伊勢市站|qid=Q6079748}} on the JR {{ill|Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023}} and the Kintetsu Yamada Line.<ref name="tm"/><ref name="rb"/>
* About a 5-minute walk from the Outer Shrine Kita-mikado entrance via {{ill|Kamiji Street|Q30114580|qid=Q30114580}}.<ref name="mr"/><ref name="rg2">JTB Publishing (2011): p. 43</ref>
* About a 3-minute walk from the Shindō bus stop (Mie Kōtsū), and immediately from the “Tsukiyomi-no-miya-mae” stop on the Ise City community bus “Okage Bus.”<ref>From July 20, 2013, Mie Kōtsū’s “Sangū Bus” stopped at the “Tsukiyomi-no-miya-mae” stop, but as of March 31, 2015, service to that stop was discontinued.</ref>
* About 3 km from the Ise Interchange on the {{ill|Ise Expressway|Q6079578|qid=Q6079578}}.
* Parking: Only 2–4 cars can park in front of the torii gate, but there are parking meters on the road to the south.
